# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

## From cand_0001
- **Total-infra-failure runs should not consume an optimizer iteration.** Here 10/10 val
  tasks failed at `docker compose build` with a Docker registry i/o timeout
  (`registry-1.docker.io`), so no skill ever executed (tool_calls=0, tokens=«redacted» The
  optimizer was still asked to "ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED fixes," but with zero
  rollouts there is nothing to diagnose or verify — any edit is a blind guess. Suggest:
  detect when ~100% of a split aborts during sandbox startup and either (a) retry the
  image pull / use a cached/pre-pulled base image, or (b) skip the optimize step and mark
  the run as environment-blocked, rather than spending an iteration that can only produce
  a no-op or a speculative regression.
- **The prompt is internally contradictory in this state.** The focus block says "seek a
  robustness/generalization gain that does not regress the solid tasks," but the same
  block lists every task as ignore-worthy infra noise and there are NO solid tasks to
  protect or generalize from. A no-signal guard that suppresses the "ship many fixes"
  framing when the split is fully infra-errored would prevent optimizers from
  over-editing blind.
- **Consider pre-pulling/mirroring base images** (e.g. a local registry mirror) so a
  transient DNS/registry outage doesn't zero an entire scoring pass.
